wang2023fragile: Relation extraction should depend on textual context, but models memorize entity-name patterns. Random and type-constrained entity replacements applied to TACRED test instances make state-of-the-art RE models lose 30 to 50 percent F1, showing they rely on names rather than context. The benchmark and code expose this brittleness and argue for RE models robust to entity substitutions.
wang2023graph: Message-passing GNNs hide topology inside feature propagation, over-relying on node features and paying high inference latency. GENN explicitly encodes graph topology using network-embedding methods as a separate information source, reducing dependence on node features, and distills an MPNN teacher into a fast student that avoids the teacher's multi-layer inference. The student runs 40 to 78 times faster, improves accuracy by over 40 percent over the teacher when node features are scarce, and even wins in feature-rich settings thanks to distillation.
wang2023primacy: Instruction-tuned models answer discriminative NLU by choosing among candidate labels listed in the prompt, raising the question of whether they inherit human cognitive biases. Experiments show ChatGPT's choice is sensitive to label order and favors labels listed earlier, a primacy effect. The findings warn that prompt formatting can skew zero-shot NLU decisions and encourage position-balanced prompting in reliable applications.
wang2024deepedit: Editing knowledge in LLMs is hard because multi-step reasoning deviates from the new fact and loses coherence. DeepEdit applies depth-first-search constrained decoding that enforces logical coherence and integrates new knowledge into reasoning, with a semantic importance estimator that ranks steps by relevance to the question. It also releases two harder benchmarks, MQuAKE-2002 and MQuAKE-Hard. Across knowledge-editing benchmarks it produces succinct, coherent reasoning chains that use the edited fact and improves quantitative accuracy.
wang2025recall: Detecting whether text appeared in an LLM's pre-training helps quantify privacy exposure, but prior membership-inference methods look at text in isolation or with non-member contexts only. Con-ReCall contrasts the distributional shift induced by a member context against that of a non-member context through contrastive decoding, amplifying subtle differences. On WikiMIA it reaches state-of-the-art membership detection and stays robust to text manipulations, showing member contexts carry signal once they are compared rather than analyzed alone.
wang2025text: ASCII art pits textual characters against the visual shapes they form. An evaluation framework using adversarial ASCII art where character-level text deliberately contradicts the global visual pattern tests five state-of-the-art VLMs including GPT-4o, Claude, and Gemini. The models consistently prioritize the text over the visual image, and visual recognition collapses as semantic complexity grows; tuning and prompt engineering only help marginally. The text-priority bias exposes a multimodal integration flaw and a risk for content moderation.
wang2025tricking: RAG systems trust external corpora, so poisoned passages can hijack retrieval. Existing poisoning attacks need retriever gradients, inversion models, or heavy compute. DIGA is a black-box attack that exploits two retriever quirks: insensitivity to token order and bias toward influential tokens. It runs a genetic algorithm whose operations adaptively focus on influential tokens, generating effective adversarial passages with far less time and memory. Across datasets it matches or beats prior attacks in success rate while being much more efficient and scalable.
wang2025vulnerability: Most jailbreak research makes input snippets more complex and hidden, but this work shows position matters more. Placing a simple, readable adversarial snippet at the start of the model's output, by directly forcing the target output prefix, exposes safety defenses far more effectively than input-suffix attacks or prompt-based output jailbreaks. The result shows that controlling where adversarial text appears, not how obfuscated it is, determines jailbreak success, with implications for output-side defenses.
wang2026highlightbench: Visual highlights, underlines, and bold text in tables are explicit directives, but existing benchmarks cannot tell whether a VLM fails to see a markup or fails to reason with it. HighlightBench splits markup-driven table understanding into five task families: markup grounding, constrained retrieval, local relations, aggregation and comparison, and consistency and missingness, and ships a reference pipeline that exposes intermediate decisions. Experiments show strong models remain unstable when visual cues must align with structured symbolic reasoning, pinpointing the perception-to-execution failure chain.
wang2026readable: Can a VLM predict what a 180-degree rotation reveals without seeing the rotated image? RotOutBench pairs original and rotated images across open visual cases and controlled text rotations. Models often read either image correctly when shown, yet fail to infer the rotated result from the original alone; on controlled text rotations predicted-rotation accuracy collapses near zero even for accurate direct readers. Diagnostics show the internal state can approach the rotated-image reading state while the final readout still follows the original string, exposing an action-prediction gap.
wu2025dimo: GUI grounding struggles with cluttered screens and ambiguous language. DiMo-GUI is training-free: it splits a screenshot into textual and iconic elements so a general-purpose VLM reasons about each modality separately, then, when an initial prediction is ambiguous, generates candidate focal regions around it and incrementally zooms in to refine the bounding box. This hierarchical, modality-aware refinement disambiguates crowded layouts without extra training or annotations, improving over baseline inference on standard GUI grounding benchmarks.
wu2025evostealer: Vendors sell prompt templates by showing sample images, and an attacker with only those images can steal the templates. PRISM is a benchmark of 50 templates and 450 images at easy and hard levels. EvoStealer steals templates by differential evolution without fine-tuning: MLLMs initialize and evolve populations of candidate prompts, and the system distills common offspring features into generalized templates. On open-source InternVL2-26B and closed GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, stolen templates reproduce images highly similar to the originals and generalize to new subjects, beating baselines by over 10 percent at low cost.
